forecaster_note: Southerly groundswell holding through Thursday and Friday, then the real story arrives Sunday — a 3.6ft 9s ENE (77°) pulse that lifts energy from 34 kJ this morning to 136 kJ by Sunday midday. Winds stay W offshore right through Thu–Sat mornings before swinging N/NNW and fresh on Sunday. (Surfline's Sydney Northern Beaches forecaster paragraph was unavailable this refresh — this is your agent's read of the raw Surfline model data.)

wind.summary: W offshore 12–13 gusting 23 km/h through sunrise, easing to 10 by 11am and near-glassy 3 km/h by 1pm before a light ENE sea breeze fills at 3pm

shark.summary: No shark detections or sightings logged Palm Beach → Manly in the last 24h. All five NSW feeds read live this refresh (SMART drumline 349, DPI drone 80, Surf Life Saving NSW 135, trauma 7, events 1) — zero Northern Beaches hits.

days.label: Today
days.note: Don't judge it at dawn. Energy sits at a flat 34 kJ from 8–9am then more than doubles to 80 kJ at 10am and 91 kJ by midday — the swell is filling in exactly as you'd be paddling out. Lead band is 1.9ft 9s from 179°, dead south, which is the direction that wraps badly into Dee Why, so Long Reef (2–4ft vs everyone else's 2–3ft) is the size winner. W offshore 13 gusting 23 grooms it early and drops to near-glassy by 1pm. Low tide 7:20am, filling to a 1.49m high at 2pm — 10am–12pm is the sweet spot on both counts.

swells.label: Dominant S groundswell — the problem direction here
E windswell — this is what feeds the banks

dee-why.window: 10am–12pm. Energy jumps from 34 to 84 kJ across that window and the tide is filling off the 7:20am low — you get bigger, better-shaped waves the later you leave it. Wind is lightest from 11am.

tip.label: 179° kills the Point — take the beachies
tip.text: A dead-south 9s swell doesn't wrap into the Point corner, it just runs past it. The 1.7ft 8s E band at 79° is the one actually hitting the beachie banks square, so surf the beach, not the Point. Any right that does stand up is your frontside — but don't burn the session waiting for the Point to switch on, because at 179° it won't.

swells.label: Dominant S groundswell — Long Reef sits open to it

long-reef.window: 10am–12pm on the pushing tide. Pick of the four spots today — a full foot bigger than Dee Why, Curl Curl and Manly at the same energy.

tip.label: Best call today
tip.text: This is the day Long Reef's exposure pays. The 179° south angle that ruins Dee Why Point walks straight into here, giving waist–chest instead of thigh–waist everywhere else. W wind at 266–270° is dead offshore across the bank. Backside on the lefts off the headland — commit to the drop early, the 9s period gives you a steeper wall than the size suggests.

curl-curl.window: 10am–12pm. Same size and rating as Dee Why with the same offshore — worth a look only if the Dee Why carpark tells you the banks are dud.

tip.label: Bank lottery, not a size play
tip.text: Nothing here that Dee Why doesn't already offer at the same 2–3ft and 84 kJ. Come only if you want the sandbank variety — North Curl Curl corner holds the S angle a touch better than the south end today.

swells.label: Dominant S groundswell — heavily shadowed here
E windswell — Manly's only real feed today

manly.window: Skip it unless you're already south. Smallest of the four all morning at 1–3ft.
alerts: Most shadowed spot on a 179° S swell — expect the low end of the range

tip.label: Wrong swell window
tip.text: North Steyne needs the E band to do the work today and there's only 1.7ft 8s of it. The south groundswell that's making Long Reef worth driving to is exactly the angle Manly's headland blocks. Drive north instead.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The most consistent morning of the three days — 100% consistency and steady 64–71 kJ right through 10am–12pm, no ramp to time. Single clean 3.0ft 9s south swell at 173° doing all the work (57 of the 64 kJ), with W offshore 10–11 gusting 14–19 km/h that goes near-glassy by 1pm. Same story as today: south angle means Long Reef holds the size, Dee Why Point stays quiet.

dee-why.window: Anytime 6am–1pm — offshore holds all morning and energy is flat, so there's no window to chase. Go when the tide suits (low 8:21am, high 3:08pm).

long-reef.window: Pick of the day again — solid 3–4ft with 100% consistency and W offshore right through the morning. Best clean-conditions session of the week if you can't get out Sunday.

curl-curl.window: Clean and rideable all morning, W offshore 10 km/h. A notch behind Long Reef on size.

manly.window: Cleanest it'll be all week but still the smallest — only worth it if you're surfing before work in town.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days — the numbers below are SUNDAY, which is the one to plan around. Saturday is the weakest day of the week (28–46 kJ, 1–3ft, W offshore till an E onshore fills around 1pm). Sunday a 3.6ft 9s ENE swell at 77° arrives and energy explodes from 34 kJ this morning to 136 kJ by 10am and 234 kJ by 1pm — that's your NE–ENE window. Catch: wind swings N/NNW 347–352° at 17 gusting 27 km/h, which is cross-shore at Dee Why and Manly but stays offshore at Long Reef and Curl Curl.

alerts: Sunday N/NNW wind 17 gusting 27 km/h is cross-shore here — rating drops to poor-fair after 9am
Saturday is the weakest day of the week: 2–3ft, 28–46 kJ
dee-why.window: Sunday 6–9am only, before the N wind gets up. The 77° ENE angle finally lights the Point up but the wind won't let it last.

long-reef.window: Sunday 10am–12pm — the standout session of the whole forecast. 136 kJ of 3.6ft 9s ENE with N/NNW staying offshore across the bank, and FAIR holding all morning while Dee Why and Manly deteriorate.

curl-curl.window: Sunday backup to Long Reef — N/NNW stays offshore here too and it holds FAIR all morning. Saturday it's the only spot rated FAIR every hour, if you must surf Sat.

alerts: Sunday N/NNW cross-shore from 9am — poor-fair the rest of the day
manly.window: Sunday dawn only. Once the N wind fills it's done — head to Long Reef or Curl Curl.
